classification.habitat: Dry and moist tropical habitats; often in scrub and open woodland
classification.distribution: Peninsular and central India and other tropical parts of the Indian subcontinent

identification.description: Slender twining plant with opposite leaves and characteristic aromatic roots.
identification.whole_plant: Perennial twining or trailing herb with slender stems.
identification.root: Long, slender, aromatic roots; brown externally with lighter interior.
identification.stem: Slender, flexible, often twining; young portions green to reddish-brown.
identification.leaf: Opposite, simple, entire, elliptic to ovate-lanceolate leaves.
identification.flower: Small greenish-purple to purplish flowers in axillary clusters.
identification.fruit: Paired slender follicles containing numerous seeds.
identification.seed: Small, elongated seeds with a tuft of hairs aiding dispersal.
identification.bark: Root bark is the principal crude-drug material; stem bark is not the usual drug part.

therapeutics.precautions: Use authenticated raw drug; therapeutic use should follow qualified clinical guidance.

reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Constituent profiles vary with plant material and extraction; use pharmacopoeial/authenticated material for analytical claims.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Sariva is traditionally described as cooling and is studied for phytochemical and pharmacological properties; specific clinical efficacy should not be inferred from traditional use alone.
modern_information.safety_notes: Avoid treating traditional indications as established clinical efficacy; authenticate the root drug.

exam_points: Cooling, aromatic root is a key identification feature

doctor.quick_reference: Root drug traditionally used in cooling and Pittaja presentations.
